title: Anthropic IPO
lede: Anthropic's IPO page sets out a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT, reports Q3 2026 revenue of $17.0 billion, and expects the share price to be set on November 18.

points: Q3 revenue grew more than 12x year on year, with over 11,900 customers above $100K in trailing revenue.
Adjusted operating margin was 15%, but a $21.9 billion non-cash charge drove a $23.3 billion net loss.
The roadshow began November 10, and trading is expected to start November 19.
Individual investors request shares through participating brokerages, with no guarantee of any allocation.

points.text: One commenter summarised the filings: a $70 to $78 range, an implied value near $968 billion, and $900.9 billion in compute commitments through 2045.
A sceptic reads the IPO as a sign of need, arguing a lab close to self-improving models would stay private; a reply notes both Anthropic and OpenAI burn cash.
Commenters split on the moat: one says local models will soon be good enough for most users, another that few people ever run things locally.
A worry that Series H buyers were already underwater was corrected: the bottom of the range sits about 19% above their price.
Several picked out the roadshow claim that Claude was ported from Nvidia to AMD GPUs in three days with little human help.
